raw_response:
I farm the way I have done for years: I start from what worked last year, then I adjust a little if the price of fertilizer or seed changes. On 10.1 mu, I will still keep wheat-maize as the main line, because that is the steady way here with well water. I will leave a small piece for cotton, not too much, because cotton takes more watching and my family has off-farm work. I do listen to what the dealer says and I watch the neighbors, but in the end I will put enough fertilizer so I do not lose yield. If I waste a little fertilizer, that hurts less than a poor harvest. For wheat I will feed it a bit heavier because it needs a strong start and I have irrigation. For maize I will use hybrid seed and keep fertilizer solid, especially nitrogen. For cotton I will not spread too wide; I will keep a smaller area and manage it tighter. I will use rotary tillage where it saves labor, and after wheat I will put maize in with less soil turning so I can move fast.
